title: Possessive Articles
sourceNote: The auto-captions are garbled. The full list of possessive articles and the two-step rule are clear; some of the video's example sentences could not be reconstructed, so the examples here were rebuilt from the rules (those not in the video are marked as supplementary).
objectives: I can name the possessive article for every personal pronoun
I can choose between mein and meine (etc.) according to the noun
I know the special forms euer / eure and unser / unsere
I can say who something belongs to: Das ist mein Auto.

grammar.title: What are possessive articles?
grammar.body:
Possessive articles are words like *my, your, his, her*: **mein, dein, sein, ihr ...** They show who something belongs to and they stand **before the noun**, in place of the article.

There is one possessive article for every personal pronoun (lesson 11): ich, du, er, sie, es, wir, ihr, Sie, sie.
grammar.ar: لكل ضمير شخصي أداة ملكية خاصة به.

grammar.title: Two steps: pronoun, then noun
grammar.body:
Always think of two things:

1. **Which pronoun** is the owner? (ich → *mein-*, du → *dein-*, er/es → *sein-*, sie → *ihr-*, wir → *unser-*, ihr → *euer-*, Sie → *Ihr-*, sie plural → *ihr-*)
2. **Which article does the noun have?** If it is **der** or **das**, the possessive article has **no ending**. If it is **die** (feminine) or **die** (plural), add **-e**.
grammar.ar: der / das: بدون نهاية. die (مؤنّث أو جمع): أضف e.

grammar.title: All possessive articles (nominative)
grammar.body: Left column: with der- and das-nouns. Right column: with die-nouns (feminine and plural).

examples.de: Ich bin Peter. Das ist meine Familie.
examples.en: I am Peter. This is my family.

examples.de: Das ist dein Auto. Das ist deine Familie.
examples.en: That is your car. That is your family.

examples.de: Das ist Peter. Das ist sein Auto.
examples.en: That is Peter. That is his car.

examples.de: Das ist Julia. Das ist ihre Familie.
examples.en: That is Julia. That is her family.

grammar.title: Special case: euer becomes eure
grammar.body:
With **ihr** (you, plural) the possessive article is **euer**. Before an ending you drop the **e** before the **r**: **euer Auto**, but **eure Familie** (not *euere*).

Only **unser** keeps its form: **unser Auto**, **unsere Familie**.

grammar.title: Formal Ihr and plural ihr
grammar.body: **Ihr / Ihre** with a capital I belongs to formal **Sie** (one person or many). **ihr / ihre** with a small i belongs to **sie** (she) and to **sie** (they).

examples.de: Herr Müller, ist das Ihr Auto?
examples.en: Mr Müller, is that your car?

examples.de: Das sind Laura und Antonio. Das ist ihr Haus.
examples.en: These are Laura and Antonio. That is their house.

mistakes.why: *euer* loses its middle *e* before the ending.

lines.de: Ja, das ist meine Familie. Das ist mein Haus und das ist unser Auto.
lines.en: Yes, that is my family. That is my house and that is our car.

lines.de: Und das? Ist das dein Hund?
lines.en: And that? Is that your dog?

tip: Learn the table by pronoun: mein, dein, sein, ihr, sein, unser, euer, Ihr, ihr. Then add -e for feminine and plural nouns.

comprehension.q: What are the two things to check when choosing a possessive article?
comprehension.a: The personal pronoun (the owner) and the article of the noun (der/das or die).

comprehension.q: Which ending do you add before feminine and plural nouns?
What is the possessive article of wir?
What happens to euer before an ending?

items.q: Ich habe ein Auto. Das ist ___ Auto.
Du hast eine Tasche. Das ist ___ Tasche.
Peter hat ein Haus. Das ist ___ Haus.
Das ist Anna. Das ist ___ Familie.
Wir haben ein Auto. Das ist ___ Auto.
Ihr habt eine Familie. Das ist ___ Familie.
Herr Müller, ist das ___ Auto? (Sie, formal)
Das sind Laura und Antonio. Das ist ___ Haus.

summary: There is one possessive article for each personal pronoun: mein, dein, sein, ihr, sein, unser, euer, Ihr, ihr.
Step 1: choose by the owner (pronoun). Step 2: look at the noun's article.
With der/das nouns: no ending (mein Auto). With die nouns (feminine and plural): add -e (meine Familie).
euer becomes eure; unser becomes unsere.
Ihr (capital) is formal; ihr (small) is 'her' or 'their'.
